raekoja: Town Hall Square and the Old Town

Tallinn's medieval square, surrounded by merchants' houses, with the Gothic Town Hall and the Town Council Pharmacy, one of the oldest in Europe. From here you walk the cobbled lanes of Vanalinn, the old town within the walls.
toompea: The city's upper hill, with the Estonian Parliament in the castle. Opposite stands the great Russian cathedral with onion domes, built in 1900. From the Kohtuotsa and Patkuli viewpoints you see the red roofs of the old town and the sea.
oleviste: The Gothic church with the very tall spire which in the Middle Ages was the tallest building in the world. A staircase of about 230 steps leads to the viewing platform, with a 360-degree view over the old town and the sea.
kiek: Kiek in de Kök and the bastion tunnels

A 15th-century artillery tower whose name means "peek into the kitchen": from its windows you could spy into the houses' courtyards. Underground you walk through the tunnels dug beneath the bastions, on a guided or self-guided visit.
viru: Viru Gate and St Catherine's Passage

The two towers of Viru Gate mark the historic entrance to the old town. A few steps away, in the narrow St Catherine's Passage, artisans work glass, ceramics and textiles in small workshops, with medieval tombstones on the wall.
kadriorg: The Baroque palace that Tsar Peter the Great built in 1718 for his wife Catherine, now an art museum with paintings from the 16th to the 20th century. Around it is a large park with a swan pond, flower gardens and tree-lined avenues.
kumu: A large modern building of limestone and glass holding Estonian art from the 18th century to today. A good refuge on cold or rainy days, with a café and views over Kadriorg Park.
lennusadam: The maritime museum in the great 1916 concrete hangars built for seaplanes. Inside are a submarine, an aircraft, historic boats and, moored outside, the icebreaker Suur Tõll.
telliskivi: A former industrial complex turned into Tallinn's creative quarter: murals, designer shops, galleries, cafés and bars in the old factories. On Saturdays there's usually a flea market.
kalamaja: The fishermen's quarter with colourful wooden houses, a short walk from the station. The Balti Jaam market brings together stalls of fish, vegetables, vintage goods and a street food area.
